################################################################################
# FILE: export.sh  [THIS SCRIPT — included for full context]
################################################################################

--- METADATA ---
  File name:             export.sh
  Relative path:         export.sh
  Size:                  15.6 KiB (16050 bytes)
  Last modified:         2026-10-18 09:47:24.855825925 -0400
  Permissions:           -rw-r--r--
  SHA-256:               5c7038df17c29857243ace68747bdf0dd1bab72ca760479275721de60f9c8c81
  MIME type:             text/x-shellscript

--- CONTENT ---
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# =============================================================================
# export.sh — Repository context dump for LLM consumption
#
# Usage:  bash export.sh
#         time bash export.sh
#
# Behaviour:
#   • Resolves its own location; works regardless of CWD.
#   • Silently exits if no Git repository is found at that location.
#   • Dumps all Git-tracked files (excluding docs/llm/**) to docs/llm/dump.txt.
#   • Prepends its own source to the dump (self-documentation).
#   • Emits rich per-file metadata (name, path, size, permissions, mtime, SHA-256).
#   • Includes a file-tree view of all included files.
#   • Prints the complete dump to stdout before writing the file.
# =============================================================================

set -euo pipefail
IFS=$'\n\t'

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 0. Resolve script's own directory — immune to CWD
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
SCRIPT_PATH="$(readlink -f "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")"
SCRIPT_DIR="$(dirname "$SCRIPT_PATH")"
SCRIPT_NAME="$(basename "$SCRIPT_PATH")"

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Validate: must be inside a working Git repository
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
if ! git -C "$SCRIPT_DIR" rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree &>/dev/null 2>&1; then
    exit 0
fi

# Ensure git is usable (index readable, not a bare repo, etc.)
if ! git -C "$SCRIPT_DIR" status --porcelain &>/dev/null 2>&1; then
    exit 0
fi

REPO_ROOT="$(git -C "$SCRIPT_DIR" rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null)" || exit 0

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Constants & derived paths
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
EXCLUDE_DIR="docs/llm"
OUTPUT_DIR="${REPO_ROOT}/${EXCLUDE_DIR}"
OUTPUT_FILE="${OUTPUT_DIR}/dump.txt"

TIMESTAMP="$(date --iso-8601=seconds)"
GIT_BRANCH="$(git -C "$REPO_ROOT" rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD 2>/dev/null || echo 'unknown')"
GIT_COMMIT="$(git -C "$REPO_ROOT" rev-parse HEAD 2>/dev/null || echo 'unknown')"
GIT_COMMIT_SHORT="$(git -C "$REPO_ROOT" rev-parse --short HEAD 2>/dev/null || echo 'unknown')"
GIT_COMMIT_MSG="$(git -C "$REPO_ROOT" log -1 --pretty=format:'%s' 2>/dev/null || echo 'unknown')"
GIT_COMMIT_DATE="$(git -C "$REPO_ROOT" log -1 --pretty=format:'%ci' 2>/dev/null || echo 'unknown')"
GIT_REMOTE="$(git -C "$REPO_ROOT" remote get-url origin 2>/dev/null || echo 'none')"
GIT_STATUS_SUMMARY="$(git -C "$REPO_ROOT" status --short 2>/dev/null | head -20 || echo '')"

HOSTNAME_VAL="$(hostname -f 2>/dev/null || hostname 2>/dev/null || echo 'unknown')"
USER_VAL="$(id -un 2>/dev/null || echo 'unknown')"
OS_VAL="$(uname -srm 2>/dev/null || echo 'unknown')"

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Collect tracked files, excluding the output directory
#    git ls-files guarantees only committed/staged files; no build artefacts.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
mapfile -t ALL_FILES < <(
    git -C "$REPO_ROOT" ls-files \
        --cached \
        --others \
        --exclude-standard \
        -z \
        2>/dev/null \
    | tr '\0' '\n' \
    | grep -v "^${EXCLUDE_DIR}/" \
    | sort
)

FILE_COUNT="${#ALL_FILES[@]}"

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Helper: human-readable file size
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
human_size() {
    local bytes="$1"
    if   (( bytes < 1024 ));               then printf '%d B'      "$bytes"
    elif (( bytes < 1048576 ));            then printf '%.1f KiB'  "$(echo "scale=1; $bytes/1024"       | bc)"
    elif (( bytes < 1073741824 ));         then printf '%.1f MiB'  "$(echo "scale=1; $bytes/1048576"    | bc)"
    else                                        printf '%.1f GiB'  "$(echo "scale=1; $bytes/1073741824" | bc)"
    fi
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Helper: SHA-256 of a file (portable across Linux distros)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
file_sha256() {
    local path="$1"
    if command -v sha256sum &>/dev/null; then
        sha256sum "$path" | awk '{print $1}'
    elif command -v shasum &>/dev/null; then
        shasum -a 256 "$path" | awk '{print $1}'
    else
        echo 'unavailable'
    fi
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 6. Helper: MIME type (best-effort, no error on missing tool)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
file_mime() {
    local path="$1"
    if command -v file &>/dev/null; then
        file --brief --mime-type "$path" 2>/dev/null || echo 'unknown'
    else
        echo 'unknown'
    fi
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 7. Build the tree view using 'tree' if available, else pure bash fallback
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
build_tree() {
    if command -v tree &>/dev/null; then
        # --fromfile reads the path list from stdin and renders a tree
        printf '%s\n' "${ALL_FILES[@]}" \
        | tree --fromfile -a --noreport 2>/dev/null \
        || _bash_tree
    else
        _bash_tree
    fi
}

_bash_tree() {
    # Pure-bash tree: reconstruct directory hierarchy from the flat file list
    local -A SEEN_DIRS=()
    local prev_depth=0
    local line

    for f in "${ALL_FILES[@]}"; do
        local dir parts depth i prefix
        dir="$(dirname "$f")"
        IFS='/' read -ra parts <<< "$f"
        depth=$(( ${#parts[@]} - 1 ))

        # Print intermediate directories we haven't seen yet
        local partial=""
        for (( i=0; i<depth; i++ )); do
            if [[ -z "$partial" ]]; then
                partial="${parts[$i]}"
            else
                partial="${partial}/${parts[$i]}"
            fi
            if [[ -z "${SEEN_DIRS[$partial]+_}" ]]; then
                SEEN_DIRS["$partial"]=1
                prefix="$(printf '│   %.0s' $(seq 1 $i))├── "
                printf '%s%s/\n' "$prefix" "${parts[$i]}"
            fi
        done

        # Print the file itself
        prefix="$(printf '│   %.0s' $(seq 1 $depth))└── "
        printf '%s%s\n' "$prefix" "${parts[$depth]}"
    done
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 8. Assemble the dump into a variable (stdout + file simultaneously)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
mkdir -p "$OUTPUT_DIR"

# We use a temp file to build, then atomic-rename at the end.
TMP_FILE="$(mktemp "${OUTPUT_DIR}/.dump.XXXXXX")"
trap 'rm -f "$TMP_FILE"' EXIT

# Tee everything to both stdout and the temp file
exec > >(tee "$TMP_FILE") 2>&1

# ── Preamble banner ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
cat <<BANNER
################################################################################
#                                                                              #
#   REPOSITORY CONTEXT DUMP                                                    #
#   Generated for LLM consumption — do not edit manually                       #
#                                                                              #
################################################################################

DUMP METADATA
═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  Generated at   : ${TIMESTAMP}
  Generator      : ${SCRIPT_NAME}
  Host           : ${HOSTNAME_VAL}
  User           : ${USER_VAL}
  OS             : ${OS_VAL}

REPOSITORY METADATA
═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  Repository root: ${REPO_ROOT}
  Branch         : ${GIT_BRANCH}
  Commit (full)  : ${GIT_COMMIT}
  Commit (short) : ${GIT_COMMIT_SHORT}
  Commit date    : ${GIT_COMMIT_DATE}
  Commit message : ${GIT_COMMIT_MSG}
  Remote origin  : ${GIT_REMOTE}
  Files included : ${FILE_COUNT}
  Excluded path  : ${EXCLUDE_DIR}/

GIT WORKING TREE STATUS (first 20 lines)
═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
BANNER

if [[ -n "$GIT_STATUS_SUMMARY" ]]; then
    printf '%s\n' "$GIT_STATUS_SUMMARY"
else
    echo "  (clean — no uncommitted changes)"
fi

# ── Self-documentation: dump this script first ───────────────────────────────
cat <<SELF_HEADER

################################################################################
# FILE: ${SCRIPT_NAME}  [THIS SCRIPT — included for full context]
################################################################################
SELF_HEADER

printf '\n--- METADATA ---\n'
_self_size="$(wc -c < "$SCRIPT_PATH")"
_self_mtime="$(stat --format='%y' "$SCRIPT_PATH" 2>/dev/null \
               || stat -f '%Sm' -t '%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S %z' "$SCRIPT_PATH" 2>/dev/null \
               || echo 'unavailable')"
_self_perms="$(stat --format='%A' "$SCRIPT_PATH" 2>/dev/null \
               || stat -f '%Sp' "$SCRIPT_PATH" 2>/dev/null \
               || echo 'unavailable')"
_self_sha="$(file_sha256 "$SCRIPT_PATH")"

printf '  %-22s %s\n'  "File name:"       "$SCRIPT_NAME"
printf '  %-22s %s\n'  "Relative path:"   "$(realpath --relative-to="$REPO_ROOT" "$SCRIPT_PATH" 2>/dev/null || echo "$SCRIPT_PATH")"
printf '  %-22s %s\n'  "Size:"            "$(human_size "$_self_size") (${_self_size} bytes)"
printf '  %-22s %s\n'  "Last modified:"   "$_self_mtime"
printf '  %-22s %s\n'  "Permissions:"     "$_self_perms"
printf '  %-22s %s\n'  "SHA-256:"         "$_self_sha"
printf '  %-22s %s\n'  "MIME type:"       "$(file_mime "$SCRIPT_PATH")"
printf '\n--- CONTENT ---\n'
cat "$SCRIPT_PATH"

# ── File tree ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
cat <<TREE_HEADER

################################################################################
# FILE TREE  (all ${FILE_COUNT} included files)
################################################################################
.
TREE_HEADER

build_tree
echo ""

# ── Per-file content dump ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
TOTAL_BYTES=0

for rel_path in "${ALL_FILES[@]}"; do
    abs_path="${REPO_ROOT}/${rel_path}"

    # Skip if the file no longer exists on disk (deleted but still indexed)
    [[ -f "$abs_path" ]] || continue

    # ── Metadata collection ────────────────────────────────────────────────
    file_size="$(wc -c < "$abs_path" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)"
    TOTAL_BYTES=$(( TOTAL_BYTES + file_size ))

    file_mtime="$(stat --format='%y' "$abs_path" 2>/dev/null \
                  || stat -f '%Sm' -t '%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S %z' "$abs_path" 2>/dev/null \
                  || echo 'unavailable')"

    file_perms="$(stat --format='%A' "$abs_path" 2>/dev/null \
                  || stat -f '%Sp' "$abs_path" 2>/dev/null \
                  || echo 'unavailable')"

    file_owner="$(stat --format='%U:%G' "$abs_path" 2>/dev/null \
                  || stat -f '%Su:%Sg' "$abs_path" 2>/dev/null \
                  || echo 'unavailable')"

    file_inode="$(stat --format='%i' "$abs_path" 2>/dev/null \
                  || stat -f '%i' "$abs_path" 2>/dev/null \
                  || echo 'unavailable')"

    file_links="$(stat --format='%h' "$abs_path" 2>/dev/null \
                  || stat -f '%l' "$abs_path" 2>/dev/null \
                  || echo 'unavailable')"

    file_sha="$(file_sha256 "$abs_path")"
    file_type="$(file_mime "$abs_path")"

    git_log_line="$(git -C "$REPO_ROOT" log -1 --pretty=format:'%h %ai %s' -- "$rel_path" 2>/dev/null || echo 'unavailable')"

    # ── Section header ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    printf '\n'
    printf '################################################################################\n'
    printf '# FILE: %s\n' "$rel_path"
    printf '################################################################################\n'
    printf '\n--- METADATA ---\n'
    printf '  %-22s %s\n'  "File name:"       "$(basename "$rel_path")"
    printf '  %-22s %s\n'  "Relative path:"   "$rel_path"
    printf '  %-22s %s\n'  "Absolute path:"   "$abs_path"
    printf '  %-22s %s\n'  "Size:"            "$(human_size "$file_size") (${file_size} bytes)"
    printf '  %-22s %s\n'  "Last modified:"   "$file_mtime"
    printf '  %-22s %s\n'  "Permissions:"     "$file_perms"
    printf '  %-22s %s\n'  "Owner:"           "$file_owner"
    printf '  %-22s %s\n'  "Inode:"           "$file_inode"
    printf '  %-22s %s\n'  "Hard links:"      "$file_links"
    printf '  %-22s %s\n'  "MIME type:"       "$file_type"
    printf '  %-22s %s\n'  "SHA-256:"         "$file_sha"
    printf '  %-22s %s\n'  "Last git commit:" "$git_log_line"
    printf '\n--- CONTENT ---\n'

    # ── Content emission ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
    # Binary files: emit a notice instead of raw bytes
    if [[ "$file_type" == application/octet-stream ]] \
    || [[ "$file_type" == image/* ]] \
    || [[ "$file_type" == audio/* ]] \
    || [[ "$file_type" == video/* ]] \
    || ! file --brief "$abs_path" 2>/dev/null | grep -qi 'text\|script\|xml\|json\|yaml\|svg\|source\|empty'; then
        printf '[Binary file — content omitted. Size: %s, SHA-256: %s]\n' \
            "$(human_size "$file_size")" "$file_sha"
    else
        cat "$abs_path"
        # Ensure there is always a trailing newline so the next header aligns
        [[ "$(tail -c1 "$abs_path" | wc -c)" -gt 0 ]] \
            && [[ "$(tail -c1 "$abs_path")" != $'\n' ]] \
            && printf '\n'
    fi
done

# ── Summary footer ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
cat <<FOOTER

################################################################################
# DUMP SUMMARY
################################################################################
  Files dumped   : ${FILE_COUNT}
  Total size     : $(human_size "$TOTAL_BYTES") (${TOTAL_BYTES} bytes)
  Output file    : ${OUTPUT_FILE}
  Completed at   : $(date --iso-8601=seconds)
################################################################################
# END OF DUMP
################################################################################
FOOTER

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 9. Atomic rename — avoids partial writes being read by concurrent processes
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
mv -f "$TMP_FILE" "$OUTPUT_FILE"

################################################################################
# FILE TREE  (all 3 included files)
################################################################################
.
.
├── export.sh
├── .gitignore
└── README.md


################################################################################
# FILE: export.sh
################################################################################

--- METADATA ---
  File name:             export.sh
  Relative path:         export.sh
  Absolute path:         /home/kushal/src/kotlin/my-stream-of-consciousness/export.sh
  Size:                  15.6 KiB (16050 bytes)
  Last modified:         2026-10-18 09:47:24.855825925 -0400
  Permissions:           -rw-r--r--
  Owner:                 kushal:kushal
  Inode:                 67017332
  Hard links:            1
  MIME type:             text/x-shellscript
  SHA-256:               5c7038df17c29857243ace68747bdf0dd1bab72ca760479275721de60f9c8c81
  Last git commit:       5c33f93 2026-10-18 09:48:07 -0400 initialize repository

--- CONTENT ---
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# =============================================================================
# export.sh — Repository context dump for LLM consumption
#
# Usage:  bash export.sh
#         time bash export.sh
#
# Behaviour:
#   • Resolves its own location; works regardless of CWD.
#   • Silently exits if no Git repository is found at that location.
#   • Dumps all Git-tracked files (excluding docs/llm/**) to docs/llm/dump.txt.
#   • Prepends its own source to the dump (self-documentation).
#   • Emits rich per-file metadata (name, path, size, permissions, mtime, SHA-256).
#   • Includes a file-tree view of all included files.
#   • Prints the complete dump to stdout before writing the file.
# =============================================================================

IFS=$'\n\t'

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 0. Resolve script's own directory — immune to CWD
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

    exit 0
fi

if ! git -C "$SCRIPT_DIR" status --porcelain &>/dev/null 2>&1; then
    exit 0
fi

OUTPUT_FILE="${OUTPUT_DIR}/dump.txt"

TIMESTAMP="$(date --iso-8601=seconds)"
GIT_BRANCH="$(git -C "$REPO_ROOT" rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD 2>/dev/null || echo 'unknown')"
GIT_COMMIT="$(git -C "$REPO_ROOT" rev-parse HEAD 2>/dev/null || echo 'unknown')"
GIT_COMMIT_SHORT="$(git -C "$REPO_ROOT" rev-parse --short HEAD 2>/dev/null || echo 'unknown')"
GIT_COMMIT_MSG="$(git -C "$REPO_ROOT" log -1 --pretty=format:'%s' 2>/dev/null || echo 'unknown')"
GIT_COMMIT_DATE="$(git -C "$REPO_ROOT" log -1 --pretty=format:'%ci' 2>/dev/null || echo 'unknown')"
GIT_REMOTE="$(git -C "$REPO_ROOT" remote get-url origin 2>/dev/null || echo 'none')"
GIT_STATUS_SUMMARY="$(git -C "$REPO_ROOT" status --short 2>/dev/null | head -20 || echo '')"

HOSTNAME_VAL="$(hostname -f 2>/dev/null || hostname 2>/dev/null || echo 'unknown')"
USER_VAL="$(id -un 2>/dev/null || echo 'unknown')"
OS_VAL="$(uname -srm 2>/dev/null || echo 'unknown')"

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

#    git ls-files guarantees only committed/staged files; no build artefacts.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
mapfile -t ALL_FILES < <(
    git -C "$REPO_ROOT" ls-files \
        --cached \
        --others \
        --exclude-standard \
        -z \
        2>/dev/null \
    | tr '\0' '\n' \
    | grep -v "^${EXCLUDE_DIR}/" \
    | sort
)

FILE_COUNT="${#ALL_FILES[@]}"

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Helper: human-readable file size
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
human_size() {
    local bytes="$1"
    if   (( bytes < 1024 ));               then printf '%d B'      "$bytes"
    elif (( bytes < 1048576 ));            then printf '%.1f KiB'  "$(echo "scale=1; $bytes/1024"       | bc)"
    elif (( bytes < 1073741824 ));         then printf '%.1f MiB'  "$(echo "scale=1; $bytes/1048576"    | bc)"
    else                                        printf '%.1f GiB'  "$(echo "scale=1; $bytes/1073741824" | bc)"
    fi
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Helper: SHA-256 of a file (portable across Linux distros)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
file_sha256() {
    local path="$1"
    if command -v sha256sum &>/dev/null; then
        sha256sum "$path" | awk '{print $1}'
    elif command -v shasum &>/dev/null; then
        shasum -a 256 "$path" | awk '{print $1}'
    else
        echo 'unavailable'
    fi
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 6. Helper: MIME type (best-effort, no error on missing tool)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
file_mime() {
    local path="$1"
    if command -v file &>/dev/null; then
        file --brief --mime-type "$path" 2>/dev/null || echo 'unknown'
    else
        echo 'unknown'
    fi
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 7. Build the tree view using 'tree' if available, else pure bash fallback
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
build_tree() {
    if command -v tree &>/dev/null; then
        # --fromfile reads the path list from stdin and renders a tree
        printf '%s\n' "${ALL_FILES[@]}" \
        | tree --fromfile -a --noreport 2>/dev/null \

_bash_tree() {

    local line

    done

cat <<SELF_HEADER

################################################################################

################################################################################

printf '\n--- METADATA ---\n'
_self_size="$(wc -c < "$SCRIPT_PATH")"
_self_mtime="$(stat --format='%y' "$SCRIPT_PATH" 2>/dev/null \
               || stat -f '%Sm' -t '%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S %z' "$SCRIPT_PATH" 2>/dev/null \
               || echo 'unavailable')"
_self_perms="$(stat --format='%A' "$SCRIPT_PATH" 2>/dev/null \
               || stat -f '%Sp' "$SCRIPT_PATH" 2>/dev/null \
               || echo 'unavailable')"
_self_sha="$(file_sha256 "$SCRIPT_PATH")"

printf '  %-22s %s\n'  "File name:"       "$SCRIPT_NAME"
printf '  %-22s %s\n'  "Relative path:"   "$(realpath --relative-to="$REPO_ROOT" "$SCRIPT_PATH" 2>/dev/null || echo "$SCRIPT_PATH")"
printf '  %-22s %s\n'  "Size:"            "$(human_size "$_self_size") (${_self_size} bytes)"
printf '  %-22s %s\n'  "Last modified:"   "$_self_mtime"
printf '  %-22s %s\n'  "Permissions:"     "$_self_perms"
printf '  %-22s %s\n'  "SHA-256:"         "$_self_sha"
printf '  %-22s %s\n'  "MIME type:"       "$(file_mime "$SCRIPT_PATH")"
printf '\n--- CONTENT ---\n'
cat "$SCRIPT_PATH"

# ── File tree ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
cat <<TREE_HEADER

################################################################################
# FILE TREE  (all ${FILE_COUNT} included files)
################################################################################
.
TREE_HEADER

build_tree
echo ""

# ── Per-file content dump ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
TOTAL_BYTES=0

for rel_path in "${ALL_FILES[@]}"; do
    abs_path="${REPO_ROOT}/${rel_path}"

    # Skip if the file no longer exists on disk (deleted but still indexed)
    [[ -f "$abs_path" ]] || continue

    # ── Metadata collection ────────────────────────────────────────────────
    file_size="$(wc -c < "$abs_path" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)"
    TOTAL_BYTES=$(( TOTAL_BYTES + file_size ))

    file_mtime="$(stat --format='%y' "$abs_path" 2>/dev/null \
                  || stat -f '%Sm' -t '%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S %z' "$abs_path" 2>/dev/null \
                  || echo 'unavailable')"

    file_perms="$(stat --format='%A' "$abs_path" 2>/dev/null \
                  || stat -f '%Sp' "$abs_path" 2>/dev/null \
                  || echo 'unavailable')"

    file_owner="$(stat --format='%U:%G' "$abs_path" 2>/dev/null \
                  || stat -f '%Su:%Sg' "$abs_path" 2>/dev/null \
                  || echo 'unavailable')"

    file_inode="$(stat --format='%i' "$abs_path" 2>/dev/null \
                  || stat -f '%i' "$abs_path" 2>/dev/null \
                  || echo 'unavailable')"

    file_links="$(stat --format='%h' "$abs_path" 2>/dev/null \
                  || stat -f '%l' "$abs_path" 2>/dev/null \
                  || echo 'unavailable')"

    file_sha="$(file_sha256 "$abs_path")"
    file_type="$(file_mime "$abs_path")"

    git_log_line="$(git -C "$REPO_ROOT" log -1 --pretty=format:'%h %ai %s' -- "$rel_path" 2>/dev/null || echo 'unavailable')"

    # ── Section header ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    printf '\n'
    printf '################################################################################\n'
    printf '# FILE: %s\n' "$rel_path"
    printf '################################################################################\n'
    printf '\n--- METADATA ---\n'
    printf '  %-22s %s\n'  "File name:"       "$(basename "$rel_path")"
    printf '  %-22s %s\n'  "Relative path:"   "$rel_path"
    printf '  %-22s %s\n'  "Absolute path:"   "$abs_path"
    printf '  %-22s %s\n'  "Size:"            "$(human_size "$file_size") (${file_size} bytes)"
    printf '  %-22s %s\n'  "Last modified:"   "$file_mtime"
    printf '  %-22s %s\n'  "Permissions:"     "$file_perms"
    printf '  %-22s %s\n'  "Owner:"           "$file_owner"
    printf '  %-22s %s\n'  "Inode:"           "$file_inode"
    printf '  %-22s %s\n'  "Hard links:"      "$file_links"
    printf '  %-22s %s\n'  "MIME type:"       "$file_type"
    printf '  %-22s %s\n'  "SHA-256:"         "$file_sha"
    printf '  %-22s %s\n'  "Last git commit:" "$git_log_line"
    printf '\n--- CONTENT ---\n'

    # ── Content emission ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
    # Binary files: emit a notice instead of raw bytes
    if [[ "$file_type" == application/octet-stream ]] \
    || [[ "$file_type" == image/* ]] \
    || [[ "$file_type" == audio/* ]] \
    || [[ "$file_type" == video/* ]] \
    || ! file --brief "$abs_path" 2>/dev/null | grep -qi 'text\|script\|xml\|json\|yaml\|svg\|source\|empty'; then
        printf '[Binary file — content omitted. Size: %s, SHA-256: %s]\n' \
            "$(human_size "$file_size")" "$file_sha"
    else
        cat "$abs_path"
        # Ensure there is always a trailing newline so the next header aligns
        [[ "$(tail -c1 "$abs_path" | wc -c)" -gt 0 ]] \
            && [[ "$(tail -c1 "$abs_path")" != $'\n' ]] \
            && printf '\n'
    fi
done

# ── Summary footer ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
cat <<FOOTER

################################################################################
# DUMP SUMMARY
################################################################################
  Files dumped   : ${FILE_COUNT}
  Total size     : $(human_size "$TOTAL_BYTES") (${TOTAL_BYTES} bytes)
  Output file    : ${OUTPUT_FILE}
  Completed at   : $(date --iso-8601=seconds)
################################################################################
# END OF DUMP
################################################################################
FOOTER

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 9. Atomic rename — avoids partial writes being read by concurrent processes
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
mv -f "$TMP_FILE" "$OUTPUT_FILE"

# My Stream Of Consciousness

> This project contains code generated by LLMs. Treat it as experimental.

My stream of consciousness 
is an android app 
where you can message yourself 
and synchronize your messages with a git remote

The goal here is to present a simple chat like interface for the user. 
Each app installation only deals with a single git remote 
most likely github dot com but it could be any git remote 
that the user can reach over the network 
the app should be resilient 
if the remote is not immediately available, 
don't be obnoxious 
show a discreet little message saying synchronization is not currently possible 
keep trying with exponential backoff 
or subscribe to network changes or whatever if possible 
try to not destroy the user's battery 
try to use engineering best practices 
solid principles 
always use latest versions of dependencies 
and latest versions of github actions 
this application will ONLY run on android 
do NOT do any cross platform nonsense like xamarin expo  or whatever 
also this app will NEVER be put on Google Play Store 
so we should support everything Android 12 and above 
why android 12 and above? 
so we can support automatic updates with obtainium and the likes 
if this assumption is incorrect, use your best judgment to support the lowest version of Android possible 
remember, we do not need to support google play store
that being said 
see if you can somehow send the latest apk that github releases generates to google play safety or bla bla
so users don't see the dreaded safety warning 
also every single push to the main branch should create a new FULL release with an APK and everything 
this project will be hosted at https://github.com/kusl/my-stream-of-consciousness
this repository is public and available free of cost 
replace this readme file with a better version when delivering changes 
always make sure this readme is upto date with the latest code changes where possible 
Use your best judgment
If only a few files (under five or there about) need to change, give me the full path of the files that need to change and the FULL file 
if there are a lot of files that need to change 
    Delivery
    Whole project as one tar.gz, unambiguous file placement
    Any files to delete on updates called out explicitly
No bespoke sed/patch scripts — full files only for anything that changes
Docs updated alongside code changes
Low verbosity, no code comments
I can't emphasize this 
NO CODE COMMENTS 
I have a small `export.sh` here with this repository 
that creates a `dump.txt` file 
which I will upload to the Claude project. 
Read this file every time 
and now you know why it is important to not add too much nonsense in the code 
the code should ideally fit within claude project without spilling over to "search mode" 
or worse without fitting in the project memory at all 
so please be concise 
we will need to somehow bundle our own version of libgit or whatever 
this kind of code that we don't edit should not be in our dump dot txt 
users will somehow need to provide their credentials to this git remote 
I don't know if there is a standard way to do this or if different forges handle this differently 
do not assume the git remote is private or public or whatever 
it is just a git remote 
do not assume anything beyond what we know 
so there are two git repositories in play here 
one is the repository for our own code 
and the other is the repository that our user uses 
we will never ever ask for general storage permission 
we will only use app scoped storage 
we only need to support a single git remote for the user's messages 
right now we will only support whatever is default so I think SHA-1
later, we will support whatever is default like SHA-256 
try to not add too many unnecessary dependencies 
definitely do not use any non-free dependencies 
I already have keystore files from an existing project which I will reuse 
https://github.com/kusl/myweather 
these password and keystore files need to always be ignored in git

so bottom line, 
use best engineering practices, 
solid principles, 
latest versions of native android strategy such as kotlin compose 
and only use performant native code 
but support being installed older versions of android as much as possible 
the diary we build is for append only 
there is no need to support editing existing entries 
we will not require the users to install any other dependencies 
the app should be fully self contained 
the text editor is fully plain text only -- UTF 8 I guess so we can support emoji
no support for markdown or anything like that 
each entry is its own timestamped file
and the interface shown to the user is like chat bubbles and a textbox 
but the chatbox can get bigger if the user keeps typing or pastes a long message 
because the file is plain text I don't think a user can type too much 
so we will be generous with file sizes 
if the message content is longer than 100KiB 
we should display the file size real if possible approximate if not possible 
if the message content is longer than 1 MiB 
the message should be in red because I mean nobody is going to read
more than 1 MiB of plain text. 
don't say this to the user but they probably belong in a mental asylum 
if they type 1 MB of stream of consciousness 
realistically it should be multiple streams of consciousness 
now here is the difficult part 
we can't just keep pushing to the remote 
we have to also fetch and pull from the remote 
always use rebase 
and always use theirs as strategy 
if we structure our files inside a specific folder in the git repository 
I think there should never be a git conflict 
but it is important to respect the remote 
and discard local changes if there are conflicts 
so that's why we start a new timestamped file each time 
add proper automated testing support as per android best engineering practices 
remember all tests need to be able to run on free tier github dot com actions public repository

does this make sense so far? 
What changes would you make to this?
